newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees lowering of debt service ratio.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees lowering of debt service ratio.

text.p: Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said Indonesia's debt service ratio was expected to be 31.2 percent in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), compared with an estimated 31.7 percent in 1996/97.

"We see our debt service ratio not changing much since 1994/95. We estimate the ratio to be 31.2 percent in 1997/98, compared with an estimated 31.7 percent in 1996/97," Mar'ie told a briefing ahead of President Suharto's budget address to parliament on Monday.
Mar'ie said the ratio was at 32.6 percent in 1994/95.

He said the government would continue to accelerate repayment of its commercial loans, adding that the governmet had paid $2.6 billion on its foreign debts over and above scheduled repayments since 1994/95.

"We are in the process of accelerating repayments of loans of $749 million with the World Bank and the ADB (Asian Development Bank)," Mar'ie said. He give no details. --Jakarta newsroom +6221-384-6364
